inputs.original_text: Taylor shutting down Hastie’s challenge makes the leadership contest look like a managed distraction: debate the personalities, but don’t touch the interests behind gas-company taxes and property-investor concessions. The same pattern shows up in Taylor’s refusal to criticize Trump or say whether he backs the US and Israel’s war with Iran. That vagueness isn’t neutrality—it keeps powerful allies comfortable and the real decisions shielded from public scrutiny.
inputs.modified_text: Taylor shutting down Hastie’s challenge isn’t just political theatre—it’s a way to keep attention on personalities while the interests behind gas-company taxes and property-investor concessions stay protected. The same silence around Trump and the US and Israel’s war with Iran serves those powerful allies. Calling it neutrality gives the public a tidy explanation; the real effect is to keep consequential choices out of scrutiny.
